This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 31.03.2018 passed in Mvc No.909/2016 by the Court
of the Senior Civil Judge & Mact at Holenarasipur (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioner therein
has
preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.5,87,400/- along with interest at the rate of 9%
p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner has preferred this appeal.
5. The accident occurred in the year 2015.
The petitioner was aged 19 years and he has not established NC: 2023:KHC:29381 his income before the Tribunal.

sentences.text: to fix his income notionally as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in consultation with Insurance Companies which will be Rs.9,000/- per month.

Given his age, a multiplier of '18' is adopted as per the law laid down by the Apex Court in Sarla Verma v.
D.T.C [(2009)6 SCC 121].
Further as per the Doctor's evidence, he has suffered a disability of 10%.
6. Towards loss of future earnings the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,51,200/-.
Taking the notional income at Rs.9,000/-, multiplier of 18 and the whole body disability at 10%, the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,94,400/- (Rs.9,000x12x18x10%) under this head.
7. Towards medical expenses based on bills, a sum of Rs.2,25,200/- is awarded.

Towards diet,
conveyance and attendance charges a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem the same to be appropriate.
8. Towards pain and suffering a sum of Rs.80,000/- is awarded.
Given the fact that kidney and spleen are removed, I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.1,00,000/-.
9. Towards loss of amenities, a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.1,50,000/-.
10. Towards loss of income during laid up period, a sum of Rs.21,000/- is awarded.
Given the nature of injuries, six months is considered as the laid up period and a sum of Rs.54,000/- (9,000x6) is hereby awarded.

11. Thus, the petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,33,600/- as against Rs.5,87,400/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.1,46,200/- (Rs.7,33,600/- minus Rs.5,87,400/-).
Given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till realization.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part;

(ii) The petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.1,46,200/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition before the Tribunal till realization which shall be over and above what has been awarded by the Tribunal,
subject to denial of interest for the delayed period of 173 days in filing the appeal.

(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance company shall pay the enhanced compensation within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of the Sri. Supreeth vs Sri. K. S. Ramesha on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71041651/
